title: Sagebrush fleet protocol v1 (O6/O7 r2.3)
$comment: Frozen design: agent-autonomous-schemas.md r2.5, sha256 589730708dbc76d742f67831e2772e8f4a85fac51650640eb76fb0747c1a1bd3. Bodies by type name in $defs (sb.<name>.v1). The browser-session body is O11's, imported from O11 draft 5.1 (sha256 66755f3a1a97d060…); the three host audit bodies (audit-event, audit-checkpoint, audit-continuity) are imported from the host audit stream design d1 to d1r5; the service's audit-ack body is still absent until imported by exact revision. Validate with lib/fleet/schema.mjs (closed subset). Amended Nov 23 2026 by the owner's ruling (a Claude login is never held, sealed or relayed by the service; Claude subscriptions are host-local, signed in through Claude Code's own flow): no subscription, sealed package or package plaintext names provider claude, and there is no claude-setup-token purpose. Nor does an agent's broker list a claude-subscription right: the host-local pool is the only authority on Claude subscriptions, and the service never learns of one. An agent's client may still be claude. The agent-message and agent-reply bodies are agent-messages r6's (sha256 a372fb354232bd17fff97a7a65aac423969b87a56846c537b0676f85ba68ca90) with its deltas r7 (e118a55b), r8 (9732a889), r9 (3be5c3cc), r10 (bc918563) and r11 (sha256 c24c03c33519217dd8054294e631d926dde1c1bfe26abe756ddd99f56695b397: the closed reasons answer_lost and not_granted, and aud), imported by exact revision.

agent-fence-ack.$comment: r2.4 §3.7.4, the old host's acknowledgement (body and acceptance rules by the lease lane). host is the old host; gen = entry_gen(agent, host), its last; transfer is the SHA-256 of the transfer it answers; boot_id is the kernel's (/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id).

agent-message.$comment: agent-messages r6 (sha256 a372fb354232bd17fff97a7a65aac423969b87a56846c537b0676f85ba68ca90) §2: a person->agent message, signed by an enrolled, non-removed device of the fleet (no tier). body_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the HPKE ct (§6). The host verifies it against its pinned chain before a turn (§7).

agent-reply.$comment: agent-messages r6 §2: an agent->person record, signed by the host's cert key. kind reply carries a body (AES-256-GCM under the answered send's reply key; body_sha256 over the ct) and reason null; turn_failed and refused carry no body (body_sha256 null) and a closed reason. in_reply_to is the last verified send the turn covered (R2), or, for refused, the refused message.

agent-transfer.$comment: r2.4 §3.7.2. to_host_key is the new host certificate's fingerprint; grant is the SHA-256 of the signed bytes of to_host's grant that adds the agent; gen = entry_gen(agent, to_host). to_host != from_host and not_after_ms - at_ms <= 10 minutes are the service's checks; the new host checks neither the window nor freshness (§3.7.3 check 2).

agent-transfer-receipt.$comment: r2.4 §3.7.3. Signed by the service key in force at chain_seq (§1.7's half-open rule). transfer is the SHA-256 of the transfer's signed bytes; every field it repeats equals the transfer's.

approval.$comment: §4. subject_hash = SHA-256 of canon(subject), checked by the verifier; gen/life/question bind agent-requested approvals.

b64.$comment: variable-length base64url (ciphertext); canonical form is checked by the decoder.

b64_16.$comment: 16 bytes, canonical base64url (§1.2): 22 characters, the last with zero pad bits.

b64_32.$comment: 32 bytes: 43 characters, zero pad bits. Keys and SHA-256 values.

b64_64.$comment: 64 bytes: 86 characters, zero pad bits. Signatures.

browser-session.$comment: §3.6, O11 draft 5.1 §3 (agent-autonomous-browser-o11.md, sha256 66755f3a1a97d060…). app_session_pub is the session's X25519 key. not_before_ms <= not_after_ms <= at_ms + 12 h is checked by the channel's verifier (lib/fleet/channel).

cap_plaintext.$comment: §5.2: the sealed capability-mint plaintext, carrying the full token.

config.$comment: config_schema 1 is the host design's (host r2 §6.1), imported by exact revision when host r2-final clears. Until then only the empty object passes (§3.2).

device-chain.$comment: §2.1. Who may sign each op (tiers, recovery key, the predecessor rule) is checked by the verifier, not the schema.

execution-lease.$comment: r2.5 §3.8.2: one execution lease, signed by the lease key in force at chain_seq (§1.7a). agent, host, gen, nonce and boot_id are the request's; host_key is the verified certificate's fingerprint; request is the SHA-256 of the request's signed bytes; no wall-clock expiry (the host counts ttl_ms from when it sent the request).

host-cert.$comment: §3.1. fingerprint is the full SHA-256 value, recomputed by every verifier and refused if it differs.

host-grant.$comment: §3.2. Cross-field rules (no_expiry_ack exactly when not_after_ms is null, tags and use consistent, uniqueness) are the verifier's.

id.$comment: r2.3 §1.1: 128 random bits and 2 zero bits, lowercase base32. The same grammar as schema/tags.schema.json $defs.id.

lease-request.$comment: r2.5 §3.8.1: a host asks for an agent's execution lease. host is the signer's certified id; gen = entry_gen(agent, host); nonce is 16 bytes from the OS; boot_id is the kernel's; at_ms feeds only the service's 5-minute window.

lease_key.$comment: r2.5 §1.7a: the lease key, pinned by a native device's lease-key entry; same shape as service_key, never the same key.

name.$comment: Display names of tags and agents: exactly agent #23's tag-name grammar (§1.1).

purpose_code.$comment: v1 closed list; display strings are in schema/fleet/purpose-codes.json. A new code is a schema change, reviewed.

scope.$comment: The endpoint's scope; the service normalizes it with normPath and refuses /.agents (§3.2).

sealed-package.$comment: §7. enc_key is the recipient's X25519 key id; enc is HPKE's 32-byte encapsulated key; ct is the AEAD output (at most 16 KiB of plaintext plus the 16-byte tag).
